extracted.intended_audience: comedians, comedy writers, and performers studying deadpan/dry-humor delivery
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for performing deadpan (dry) humor: delivering absurd or charged content with emotional neutrality so the contrast between content and delivery produces comedy. Emphasizes vocal/physical minimalism, precise timing, and avoiding overt signals that a line is a joke.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emotional flatness / neutral delivery
rubrics_metrics.description: Deliberate display of emotional neutrality (or no emotion) as a form of comedic delivery; delivery is blunt, ironic, laconic, or apparently unintentional.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key characteristics include a monotonous voice, an expressionless face, and minimal body language. The neutral surface lets absurdity shine without competing. Anti-patterns: showing obvious emotion, exaggerated facial expressions, or active physicality that undercuts the deadpan effect. Examples/practitioners to model: Buster Keaton, Steven Wright, Mitch Hedberg, Bill Murray.

rubrics_metrics.name: Absurd or charged content
rubrics_metrics.description: The material itself should be absurd, ridiculous, or carry emotional/ideational charge that contrasts with the neutral delivery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comedy arises from the content being inherently absurd or unexpected; deadpan heightens this by playing it straight. Ensure the setup/context creates an expectation that can be subverted. Anti-patterns: bland content with no incongruity, or content so subtle it never registers as absurd.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discrepancy/gap between delivery and content
rubrics_metrics.description: The difference between the emotionally flat delivery and the absurd/charged content must be the source of the joke.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listener must look for humor in the contradiction between words, delivery, and context; the gap should carry the joke rather than relying on explicit cues. Evaluate whether the mismatch itself produces the intended comic effect. If the gap is too small the joke won't register; if it's incoherent the audience may be confused.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid telegraphing the punchline / do not signal 'this is a joke'
rubrics_metrics.description: The performer should not give conventional cues that a line is a joke (no telegraphing or overt prompting for laughter).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deadpan does NOT signal 'this is a joke' — the audience must catch it. Defying the cue-laughter convention increases payoff because the audience does the decoding. Anti-patterns: laugh tracks, exaggerated pauses that clearly announce a punchline, or body language that telegraphs a joke in advance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Precise timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Lines must be delivered at the right moment; timing is critical for deadpan to balance anticipation and audience comprehension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timing determines whether the contrast lands: deliver too early and the audience misses the setup; too late and the moment is lost. Evaluate rhythm, pauses, and pacing to ensure they allow the audience to decode the incongruity. Practice to achieve the delicate balance between understatement and clarity.
